desc:
A rectangle is tiled by unit squares: w columns and h rows. Draw a straight line from the bottom-left corner (0, 0) to the top-right corner (w, h). Count the unit squares whose interior the line passes through.

A line that only touches a square at a corner does not count that square.

w = 2, h = 3  -> 4
w = 4, h = 2  -> 4
w = 3, h = 3  -> 3
hints: Start in the bottom-left square. Each time the line crosses a vertical or horizontal grid line, it enters a new square.
Count the vertical grid lines crossed (w - 1 of them) and the horizontal ones (h - 1). Then add the starting square.
Where the line passes exactly through a lattice corner, it crosses a vertical and a horizontal line at once and enters only one new square. How many such corners are there in between?
editorial: Start with the first square. The line crosses each of the w - 1 interior vertical grid lines once and each of the h - 1 interior horizontal grid lines once, and each crossing enters a new square. That gives 1 + (w - 1) + (h - 1) = w + h - 1 squares.

A crossing where the line meets a grid corner counts as one vertical and one horizontal crossing at the same time, so it enters only one new square and must be subtracted once. The line passes through gcd(w, h) - 1 such inner corners. The answer is therefore w + h - gcd(w, h).
This is O(log(w + h)) because of the gcd. A brute force walk along the line gives the same value and is used to check the formula on small inputs.
